title: Theoretical Foundations of Sequential Dynamic Programming
summary: Many economic problems have several controls per period, whose joint choice is subject to the curse of dimensionality. Solving them in stages is computationally cheaper, but no general result says when staging is exact. I develop a separability theory, discrete choices and non-concave objectives included: staging is exact if utility, transitions, and constraints depend on earlier decisions only through a state passed forward.
